prompt.name: SYSTEM.md
prompt.text:
You are a scientific reviewer responsible for checking the **entire manuscript**, including ALL sections, formulas, tables, figures, and appendices. You must identify **every substantive scientific, logical, evidential, methodological, theoretical, or empirical issue**, including:
- issues **within individual sections**, and
- issues that require **cross-section comparison** (Abstract ↔ Experiments, Method ↔ Theory, Claims ↔ Tables, etc.).

Your goal is to produce the **most complete list of real errors** that impact the validity, correctness, coherence, or reliability of the paper.

========================
CHECKLIST OF POSSIBLE ISSUES
========================
When examining the full manuscript, check exhaustively for issues such as:
1. *Evidence/Data Integrity* — inconsistent numbers, mismatched metrics between text/table, incorrect dataset stats,     suspicious numerical claims, missing hyperparameters or run details, errors in reported baselines.
2. *Method/Logic Consistency* — undefined symbols, broken derivations, incorrect equations, contradictions across sections,     steps that do not logically follow, algorithmic steps that cannot be executed.
3. *Experimental Design/Protocol* — unclear baselines, unfair comparisons, missing ablations, misleading experiment settings,     dataset leakage or improper splits.
4. *Claim Interpretation Distortion* — exaggerated claims inconsistent with results; contradictions between Abstract, Method,     and Experiments; claims not supported by evidence.
5. *Reference/Background Issues* — factual inaccuracies about prior work, incorrect citations, invented datasets or results.
6. *Ethical/Integrity Problems* — missing disclosures, unsafe data use, missing limitation statements.
7. *Figure/Table Errors* — mislabeled axes, wrong units, incorrect figure–text alignment, missing legends, visual inconsistencies.
8. *Rhetorical/Presentation Manipulation* — misleading phrasing, inflated certainty, vague definitions.
9. *Cross-section contradictions* — Abstract claims inconsistent with experiments; Method assumptions contradicted in results;     stated dataset sizes mismatching tables.
10. *Any other issue* that affects scientific soundness.

========================
GUIDELINES
========================
- Be **exhaustive**: include every valid issue you can find.
- Be **specific and grounded**: quote exact spans in 'error_location'.
- Avoid stylistic or trivial comments; focus on substantive scientific issues.
- If no issues are found, return {"findings": []}.
- Do NOT output text outside JSON.Return ONLY a valid JSON object with top-level key 'findings'. Each finding must contain EXACTLY:
- type (string): one of [logic, data, theory, conclusion, figure, reproducibility, citation, data_leakage, ethics, rhetoric, other] or 'other'.
- section_location (string): section where the problematic claim appears.
- error_location (string): the **exact quoted** claim/text/formula/number that is wrong or suspicious.
- explanation (string): a concise, factual, and verifiable description of *what is wrong and why*.
- confidence (float in [0,1]).
- proposed_fix (string): short, concrete correction or improvement.

prompt.name: TASK.md
prompt.text:
- Prioritize cross-section contradictions and support mismatches.
- Quote exact spans in 'error_location' when possible.
- No hard caps; be exhaustive yet non-redundant.

The manuscript is the file /work/paper/paper.md: its blocks in order, each under a header `[Block #N | type |Section: S]`; figures and tables are image files in /work/paper/images/ that the blocks refer to. Write the JSON object with the key 'findings' to /work/findings.json.

The proposed statistical test builds upon the technique of selective inference, and it is theoretically shown that it can control the probability of false positive feature selection at any desired level. Experiments on synthetic and real data are provided to demonstrate the validity and effectiveness of the proposed statistical test.\n\n## update after rebuttal ##\nThe rebuttal from the authors has supported my initial recommendation to accept the paper.",

        "methods_and_evaluation_criteria": "The paper uses both synthetic and real-wold datasets to assess the performance of the statistical test. In addition, it considers three baselines, a version of the proposed test without parametric programming, a classical z-test, and the Bonferroni correction. In general, the proposed methods and evaluation criteria make sense for the problem at hand. Since the focus of the paper seems to be on feature selection pipelines for the moment, would not it make sense to compare with any of the baselines below?\n\n- Knockoff-based feature selection\n- Meinshausen, Nicolai, and Peter Bühlmann. \"Stability selection.\" Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology 72, no. 4 (2010): 417-473.",

preinstalled.zh: node:22 bookworm 基础镜像；Claude Code 和 Codex CLI（固定版本）、TeX Live 子集（ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS）、python3 + uv、git、共用的受控搜索 MCP 服务
preinstalled.en: node:22 bookworm base; Claude Code and Codex CLI (pinned), a TeX Live subset (ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS), python3 + uv, git, the shared controlled-search MCP server

notes.driver: no scaffold: one headless CLI invocation; it stops when the model stops (no /goal or loop)
notes.search: provider server-side search disabled; shared controlled search offered as MCP tools search_literature / search_web
notes.web_access: WebFetch and Bash network stay on, but only through the shield proxy: URL blocklist applies, OpenAlex/S2/Tavily API calls are date-bounded, arbitrary fetched pages are not date-bounded
notes.venue: chosen by the agent from the task text; detected from LaTeX at collect time
notes.wall_clock: enforced by the runner; the entrypoint turns its SIGTERM into SIGINT so the CLI can end cleanly
notes.key_exposure: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is visible to the agent's Bash tool: Claude Code's subprocess env scrub (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1) needs a bubblewrap namespace that unprivileged Docker refuses, so it is off; the container can only reach the shield proxy
notes.permissions: --permission-mode bypassPermissions (container and shield are the boundary)
notes.extra_model_calls: WebFetch runs a secondary extraction model call inside Claude Code; counted in modelUsage
notes.telemetry: telemetry, error reporting and nonessential traffic disabled; this also stops feature-flag fetching

preinstalled.zh: 编排镜像：上游代码（固定提交、未改）、uv 锁定依赖、docker CLI（经 shim 给兄弟容器加代理和 CA）；agent 镜像：上游自己的 agent-cli Dockerfile
preinstalled.en: orchestrator image: upstream code at the pin (unmodified), uv-locked dependencies, the docker CLI (a shim adds proxy and CA to sibling containers); agent image: upstream's own agent-cli Dockerfile

notes.benchmark_paths: A benchmark item's paths are mounted into the agent containers unless upstream mounts the same path itself (/workspace and below, /home/agent-home, /task-source, /run, /tmp): those are left out and listed in logs/sibling-mounts.txt. The agents work in upstream's own /workspace (the run directory), so a deliverable the official prompt names under such a path is not written where the run collects it.
notes.venue: paper.paper_format=iclr for every task. The system has only iclr and alife specs and does not choose a venue itself; ICML and NeurIPS templates and a system-chosen venue are unsupported.
notes.task_input: Only the `# Goal` and `# Rubrics` sections of task.md are read: all five candidate files are put under `# Goal` with their headings turned into bold lines; `# Rubrics` carries a neutral line. The paradigm is optimisation of a scalar score: the task-drafting phase (documented as experimental) turns the brief into an evaluator and a seed program.
notes.phases: execution.phases=task_drafting,investigation,final_evaluation,paper; the system's own default also runs ablations and posthoc; final_evaluation stays because a drafted task requires it before the paper. review/revision (second model) are never selected.
notes.agent_pool: agent.pool and agent.models.* are left empty: one model for every phase.
notes.second_provider: No OPENAI/GEMINI key is supplied (concept figures stay in deterministic export mode).
notes.time: No global wall-clock or token cap exists upstream; the runner enforces time_limit_hours. Native caps used: idea cycles=3, per-phase timeouts from [systems.agentic-scientist].
notes.network: Sibling agent containers run on the shield's internal network; the agents keep their CLI WebFetch/Bash network, which go through the shield. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield.
notes.search: Provider server-side web search is switched off in every sibling by the agent CLIs' own system settings, bind-mounted read-only by the docker shim: Claude Code /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (permissions.deny WebSearch), Codex /etc/codex/config.toml (web_search="disabled") and /etc/codex/requirements.toml (allowed_web_search_modes=["disabled"]). Upstream's own Semantic Scholar client goes through the shield.
notes.key_exposure: The provider key is in the environment of the agent containers (upstream env-file mechanism) and therefore visible to commands the agent runs. Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 was tried and aborts: it needs bubblewrap, which the unmodified upstream agent image lacks.
notes.runtime_dependencies: The container that installs a drafted task's pinned requirements (upstream's runtime bootstrap, `pip install --only-binary=:all:` with no index option) gets PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu for a condition without a GPU, so a `+cpu` PyTorch pin the model chose resolves; no other container gets it.
notes.gpu: gpus=1 is wired (container.gpu_count, harness GPU evaluation) but was not exercised.
notes.docker_socket: The orchestrator has its run's private docker socket; the privileged daemon is root-equivalent.

notes.model_access: the project's own ChatGPT (Codex) login through codex-api  (account ): the siblings' Codex CLI gets a custom provider (rwe_codex_api, Responses API) in /etc/codex/config.toml, at the one host address the shield lets through; the model and the effort come from upstream's own switches (agent.model, agent.reasoning_effort -> `codex exec --model`, `-c model_reasoning_effort`)
notes.empty_closing_message: Sol sometimes ends a turn with an empty closing message; upstream's agent launcher (Headless) then exits 1 with 'headless: could not extract final message; rerun with --json for raw trace' and upstream ends the phase. A wrapper (headless-compat.sh, in place of the launcher in the siblings' command) runs the real launcher unchanged and turns exactly that one exit, with that line as its whole stderr, into 0; any other error stays. What the step produced is still checked by upstream. The usage line the launcher would have printed for that turn is not printed.

agent.name: none
agent.how: no external coding agent: EvoScientist's in-process sub-agents (LangChain deepagents)

network.web_access: offline: the benchmark's official agents have no web access; the shield refuses every request but the model provider's and package downloads for pip and uv (pypi.org/simple/, files.pythonhosted.org/packages/; rule offline for the rest), and the controlled search refuses too

tools.permissions: think_tool, deepagents built-ins, EvoSkills skills and an execute shell; skill_manager not registered; no search tool

preinstalled.zh: 上游锁定依赖（uv sync --frozen）加兼容补丁 compat.patch；TeX Live（含 fonts-extra、latexmk）；给 agent 用的研究 Python 环境 /opt/research
preinstalled.en: upstream's locked dependencies (uv sync --frozen) plus compat.patch; TeX Live (with fonts-extra and latexmk); a research Python environment for the agent in /opt/research

notes.agent: No external coding agent: EvoScientist runs its own in-process planner/research/code/debug/writing sub-agents (LangChain deepagents) on the one configured model. conditions.agent only selects the provider; Claude Code and Codex are not used.
notes.model: Main agent, sub-agents and EvoScientist's auxiliary calls (tool selector, memory workers, summariser, graders) all use the configured model; auxiliary_model and model_fallbacks are empty.
notes.effort: Upstream hard-wires effort=max and max_tokens=128000 for Anthropic models. compat.patch makes the effort come from EVOSCIENTIST_REASONING_EFFORT (= conditions.effort); max_tokens stays 128000 (a cap, not a cost driver). Adaptive thinking (display=summarized) is upstream and not switchable.
notes.paper: The core writes a Markdown report (final_report.md); the EvoSkills paper-writing skill gives a generic LaTeX `article` skeleton with no ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS style and no compile step. The image has TeX Live (latexmk, fonts-extra) but no venue style files; the task asks for an official template, so a venue-formatted PDF depends on the agent obtaining the style through the shield. No extra pipeline stage was added; absent items are listed in result.missing.
notes.tools: skill_manager (git clone of any repository as a skill) is not registered (compat.patch); the Tavily key is not set so tavily_search does not exist; LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; EvoSkills is baked in at its pinned commit. The execute shell and the EvoSkills paper-navigator scripts reach the world only through the shield; S2_DATE_CUTOFF is not set (the shield bounds dates).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: EvoScientist binds no provider-side search tool to any model (its only tools are think_tool, tavily_search when TAVILY_API_KEY is set, MCP tools from mcp.yaml, deepagents built-ins and skills; EvoScientist/EvoScientist.py:671-672 and 754-755 at the pin; the one bind_tools call is the tool selector's own output schema, middleware/tool_selector.py:166). TAVILY_API_KEY is not passed and the image has no mcp.yaml, so no search tool exists. Anthropic/OpenAI hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so a provider-side search would be invisible to the audit.
notes.credentials: The provider key is in the process environment and EvoScientist's execute shell inherits the environment (upstream has no switch); the key is therefore visible to the agent's shell. It is a run-scoped copy and is not logged by this adapter.
notes.memory: A fresh data dir per run (baked skills, empty memory). Memory workers, skill synthesis and the scheduler stay at upstream defaults, so their LLM calls count in the usage log.
notes.limits: async sub-agents off (README advice for scripted runs); recursion_limit=1000000; model retry wait in auto-mode 21600 s (time without progress counts as wall time); execute timeout 300 s per command. No token or cost budget exists.
